title: Changes in spinal stiffness with chronic thoracic pain: correlation with pain and muscle activity
author: Isabelle Pagé
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.twwepfe

steps.title: Obtain consent and ID data
steps.instruction: At the start of the first session, give the participant the information sheet, answer any questions, obtain a written consent, and record age, sex, weight, height, and thoracic back‑pain history on the identification sheet.

steps.title: Physical exam and eligibility screening
steps.instruction: Conduct a short physical examination and administer eligibility questionnaires (approximately 20 minutes) to confirm that the participant meets inclusion criteria and has no exclusion criteria.

steps.title: Administer study questionnaires
steps.instruction: Have the participant complete the Quebec Back Pain Disability Scale (QBPDS), Tampa Scale for Kinesiophobia (TSK), 101‑point Visual Analogue Scale (VAS), STarT Back Screening Tool (SBT), pain‑body diagram, and expectations questionnaire (≈10 minutes).

steps.title: Prepare skin for EMG
steps.instruction: Shave the skin over the erector spinae, gently abrade with soft‑grade sandpaper (Red Dot Trace Prep, 3 M, St. Paul, MN, USA), and clean with alcohol swabs (≈5 minutes).

steps.title: Place EMG electrodes and accelerometers
steps.instruction: Position surface EMG electrodes bilaterally over the erector spinae 2 cm lateral to the T5 and T8 spinous processes and at the T6/T7 inter‑spinous space; attach Delsys accelerometers to record vertebral displacement.

steps.title: Randomize spinal level order
steps.instruction: Generate a random sequence for the four thoracic levels (T5, T6, T7, T8) to be tested during the session.

steps.title: Measure spinal stiffness
steps.instruction: For each level in the randomized order, perform four consecutive stiffness trials using the servo‑linear motor device with a 2 cm‑diameter cylindrical indenter covered by rubber; apply a 45 N load to the spinous process for less than 10 seconds while recording sEMG and accelerometer data, then allow a 1‑minute rest before the next trial.

substeps.instruction: Set device to 45 N constant force.
Apply force for <10 s and record data.
Wait 1 min before the next trial.

steps.title: Collect pain intensity ratings
steps.instruction: Immediately after each stiffness assessment (and after any spinal manipulative therapy, if performed), ask the participant to rate pain on a 0‑to‑100 oral scale.

steps.title: Optional fourth‑group repeat assessment
steps.instruction: For participants in the added fourth group (first three sessions only), after the initial stiffness assessment at a level, wait 5 minutes, then repeat the stiffness assessment at the same level (no spinal manipulative therapy is delivered). The fourth session follows the standard protocol used for the other groups.

substeps.instruction: Perform first stiffness assessment as described.
Perform a second stiffness assessment at the same level.

steps.title: Compensate participant and conclude session
steps.instruction: At the end of the first session, give the participant $25 as compensation and thank them for participation.
